description: All India Debt & Investment Survey (AIDIS), NSSO/MoSPI -- the land/asset/debt-by-caste data the project brief called for as a genuine wealth/financial-strength metric, distinct from MPCE consumption (data/raw/consumption/) and from enrollment/employment share. National (All-India) figures only, consistent with this project's national-only v1 scope.
scope_note: Asset holdings (AVA) by social group are only available as a single snapshot (2019) -- the prior AIDIS round's summary report (2012-13, NSS KI 70/18.2) breaks assets down by occupational category (cultivator/non-cultivator, self-employed/others) and by decile class, but NOT by social group. Debt (IOI/AOD) by social group IS available for both rounds, giving a genuine 2-point trend. This asymmetry is real, not an oversight -- flagged explicitly rather than forcing a fabricated 2012-13 asset-by-social-group figure.

tables_used.debt: Statement 3.9 (Chapter 3, page 29): IOI and AOD by Social Groups as on 30.06.2018.

2012_13.publisher: National Sample Survey Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation

tables_used.debt: Statement 3.6 (Chapter 3, page 17): Incidence of indebtedness (IOI) and average debt per household (AOD) by social group of household, all-India.

assets_2019_rs.note: Average Value of Assets (AVA) per household, in rupees. Single snapshot only -- see scope_note.

debt_by_year.note: Incidence of Indebtedness (IOI, % of households with outstanding cash debt) and Average Amount of Debt (AOD, Rs. per household). A LOW IOI/AOD for a group is not necessarily 'financially healthy' -- combined with a low asset base (as with ST), it more plausibly reflects exclusion from formal/informal credit markets rather than an absence of need for credit. This is flagged explicitly in the UI, not left to be misread as a positive.

debt_asset_ratio_2019_pct.note: DAR = AOD as a percentage of AVA, same households, same date (30.06.2018). Single snapshot only.
